benchmarks.notes: World Bank says ~7.8% average growth is needed to reach high-income status by 2047; FY2025-26 provisional real GDP growth is 7.7%.
Economic Survey states investment rate must rise to ~35% of GDP from ~31%.
Economic Survey estimates 78.5 lakh new non-farm jobs needed annually until 2030.
Record total exports in FY2025-26. No single 2047 export target entered.
Economic Survey identifies 100% literacy as necessary for Viksit Bharat.
Monthly PLFS: female LFPR 32.7% in June 2026.
Viksit Bharat vision is commonly framed as zero poverty; NITI estimate is 11.28% in 2022-23.

benchmarks.indicator: PMAY-G houses completed vs allocated target
benchmarks.notes: 3.12 crore completed against cumulative target allocation of 4.18 crore as of 3 Aug 2026.
India crossed 300 GW non-fossil capacity; 500 GW target for 2030.

benchmarks.indicator: Non-fossil share of installed power capacity
benchmarks.notes: 50% installed-capacity milestone was reached in June 2025, ahead of the 2030 NDC timeline.
Net-zero target is 2070.
NITI's DPI@2047 roadmap frames DPI as a core enabler of inclusive socioeconomic growth.

benchmarks.indicator: Ease of doing business / regulatory simplification
benchmarks.notes: NITI emphasizes simplifying regulations, single-window systems, and periodic regulatory review.
NITI identifies cybersecurity and digital resilience as a core component of national security.
MY Bharat had more than 2.22 crore youth registrations as of July 2026.
PIB reported over 2.3 lakh recognised startups in June 2026.
Rural development backgrounder reports 10.05 crore women mobilised across 90.09 lakh SHGs.
Government backgrounder cites extreme poverty at 5.3% in 2022-23.
ViksitIndia compiles a roughly US$30–40tn 2047 ambition from various sources; treat as a broader vision benchmark.
ViksitIndia compiles a 2047 per-capita-income ambition around US$15k–18k; editable benchmark.

initiatives.name: Make in India
initiatives.progress: Tracks manufacturing competitiveness, FDI, sectoral investment and linked industrial programmes.
initiatives.target: Strengthen manufacturing, investment, exports and global value-chain participation.
initiatives.latest: PLI schemes are a major linked implementation instrument; as of 31 Mar 2026, PLI sectors had attracted over ₹2.40 lakh crore in actual investment and generated over 14.15 lakh jobs.

children.name: Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes
children.budget: ₹1.91 lakh crore approved outlay across 14 sectors
children.spent: Incentive disbursement varies by sector; not treated here as equivalent to total investment.
children.progress: Over ₹2.40 lakh crore actual investment; 14.15 lakh+ direct and indirect jobs; ₹15.2 lakh crore+ exports as of 31 Mar 2026.
children.target: Expand domestic manufacturing capacity and global competitiveness.
children.latest: Government reported strong investment, employment and export gains across PLI sectors in July 2026.

initiatives.name: Aatmanirbhar Bharat
initiatives.progress: Implemented through multiple sectoral, industrial, infrastructure, MSME, welfare and resilience programmes.
initiatives.target: Build domestic capacity and reduce critical external vulnerabilities.
initiatives.latest: Tracked here as an umbrella; linked programmes are shown separately where they have identifiable budgets and metrics.

initiatives.name: Startup India
initiatives.progress: Startup India provides recognition, regulatory support, funding access, mentorship and market-access instruments.
initiatives.target: Strengthen India's startup and innovation ecosystem.
initiatives.latest: Startup India continues to operate through instruments such as Fund of Funds, Seed Fund and Credit Guarantee Scheme.

children.name: Fund of Funds for Startups (FFS)
children.spent: Current SIDBI commitment/disbursement series should be updated from the latest SIDBI/DPIIT reporting.
children.progress: Provides capital to SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Funds that invest in startups.
children.target: Catalyse domestic venture-capital investment.
children.latest: Startup India continues to list FFS as a core scaling-stage funding instrument.

children.name: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS)
children.spent: Disbursed through selected incubators; cumulative expenditure should be refreshed from scheme reporting.
children.progress: Designed to support proof of concept, prototype development, product trials, market entry and commercialisation.
children.target: Support about 3,600 entrepreneurs through 300 incubators.
children.latest: The scheme's final application/selection cycle was extended into 2026.

children.name: Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups (CGSS)
children.budget: Guarantee framework rather than grant outlay
children.spent: Guarantees are extended through eligible member institutions.
children.progress: Current framework allows guarantee coverage on eligible startup debt up to ₹20 crore per borrower, subject to scheme conditions.
children.target: Improve collateral-free debt access for DPIIT-recognised startups.
children.latest: Revised framework increased the maximum eligible debt coverage per borrower.

initiatives.name: Skill India Mission
initiatives.progress: MSDE delivers skilling through PMKVY, Jan Shikshan Sansthan, NAPS and Craftsmen Training Scheme/ITIs.
initiatives.target: Skill, reskill and upskill the workforce with industry-relevant capabilities.
initiatives.latest: Government reaffirmed the four-scheme delivery structure in July 2026.

children.name: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)
children.budget: Scheme-specific budget; current allocation to be refreshed from Union Budget/MSDE
children.spent: Current expenditure to be refreshed from MSDE/Union Budget reporting
children.progress: Flagship short-term skilling and recognition-of-prior-learning programme.
children.target: Industry-aligned skilling and employability.
children.latest: PMKVY remains one of the principal Skill India delivery schemes.

children.name: Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS)
children.spent: Current expenditure to be refreshed from MSDE reporting
children.progress: Community-based vocational training, especially for disadvantaged groups.
children.target: Expand accessible livelihood-oriented skills.
children.latest: Listed by MSDE as a core Skill India delivery scheme in 2026.

children.name: National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS)
children.spent: Current expenditure to be refreshed from MSDE reporting
children.progress: Supports apprenticeship training with employers.
children.target: Expand work-based learning and industry training.
children.latest: Listed by MSDE as a core Skill India delivery scheme in 2026.

children.name: Craftsmen Training Scheme / ITIs
children.spent: Tracked through DGT/MSDE allocations
children.progress: Delivers trade-based vocational training through Industrial Training Institutes.
children.target: Build job-ready technical skills.
children.latest: MSDE continues to identify CTS through ITIs as a principal Skill India channel.

initiatives.name: Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat)
initiatives.ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports / Department of Youth Affairs
initiatives.budget: Budgeted through the Department of Youth Affairs / MY Bharat activities
initiatives.spent: National cumulative expenditure not inserted; state-level utilisation is reported in parliamentary replies.
initiatives.progress: 2.46 crore+ youth registered; 1.22 lakh+ enrolled in nearly 25,000 Experiential Learning Programmes as of Aug 2026.
initiatives.target: Expand volunteering, experiential learning, leadership, skilling and civic participation.
initiatives.latest: AI CV tools, CSC integration and experiential-learning programmes were expanded in 2026.

initiatives.name: National Education Policy 2020
initiatives.spent: Implemented through multiple education schemes and reforms
initiatives.progress: Implemented through school, higher-education, digital, literacy and teacher-development initiatives.
initiatives.target: Transform access, quality, flexibility, foundational learning and multidisciplinary education.
initiatives.latest: Ministry of Education's Aug 2026 implementation update lists PM SHRI, NIPUN Bharat, ULLAS, APAAR, SWAYAM Plus and other reforms.

children.name: PM SHRI
children.ministry: Ministry of Education / Department of School Education & Literacy
children.budget: ₹27,360 crore total project cost; ₹18,128 crore Central share for 2022-23 to 2026-27
children.spent: Track via annual PAB-approved outlays; central approved outlay for 2026-27 reported at ₹5,224 crore.
children.progress: 13,092 schools selected as of Jul 2026, about 90% of the 14,500+ target.
children.target: Develop 14,500+ exemplar schools aligned with NEP 2020.
children.latest: Government published an updated PM SHRI progress review in Sep 2026.

children.name: NIPUN Bharat
children.ministry: Ministry of Education / Department of School Education & Literacy
children.budget: Implemented under Samagra Shiksha rather than a standalone budget line
children.spent: Track under Samagra Shiksha FLN expenditure
children.progress: All States/UTs are implementing the foundational literacy and numeracy mission.
children.target: Universal foundational literacy and numeracy in the foundational grades.
children.latest: Government issued a detailed NIPUN Bharat implementation update in Jul 2026.

children.name: ULLAS / New India Literacy Programme
children.budget: ₹1,037.90 crore total outlay for FY2022-23 to FY2026-27
children.spent: Central and state spending tracked under the scheme; cumulative utilisation to be refreshed from latest reporting.
children.progress: Targets adult foundational literacy, critical life skills, basic education, vocational skills and continuing education.
children.target: 5 crore learners over the scheme period.
children.latest: ULLAS remains a named NEP implementation initiative in the 2026 education update.

children.name: APAAR
children.spent: Implemented within education digital systems
children.progress: Provides a lifelong academic identity to track student educational journeys and achievements.
children.target: Enable portable, interoperable academic records.
children.latest: Listed by the Ministry as a major higher-education implementation reform in Aug 2026.

children.name: SWAYAM Plus

children.progress: 500+ courses from 89 industry partners across 17 sectors; 6 lakh+ registrations reported in Aug 2026.

children.latest: Ministry of Education reported continued expansion in Aug 2026.

initiatives.name: Digital India

children.progress: 2.21 lakh Gram Panchayats reported service-ready by Aug 2026.

initiatives.name: PM GatiShakti National Master Plan
initiatives.spent: N/A — projects are funded by the implementing ministries and states
initiatives.progress: 396 infrastructure projects worth about ₹18.66 lakh crore evaluated; 256 sanctioned and 198 under implementation as of Aug 2026.
initiatives.latest: 58 Central ministries/departments and all 36 States/UTs were onboarded; the public platform expanded access to analytics.

initiatives.name: PM Awas Yojana - Gramin
initiatives.spent: ₹2,17,896.40 crore spent over FY2021-22 to FY2025-26 including Central and State shares; ₹1,31,100.02 crore Central share released over that period.

initiatives.latest: 79 lakh sanctioned houses remained under construction in Aug 2026.

initiatives.name: Ayushman Bharat
initiatives.spent: Tracked through PM-JAY claims and health-system component spending
initiatives.progress: Combines primary-care transformation with publicly financed hospital coverage.
initiatives.target: Improve access to primary, secondary and tertiary healthcare while reducing out-of-pocket costs.
initiatives.latest: By Aug 2026, more than 1.86 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs were functional; PM-JAY had authorised 12.69 crore hospital admissions worth ₹1.92 lakh crore by 30 Jun 2026.

children.spent: ₹1.92 lakh crore in authorised hospital admissions as of 30 Jun 2026; this is value of authorised care, not identical to budget expenditure.

children.target: ₹5 lakh per family per year for eligible secondary and tertiary hospital care, with later coverage expansions.

children.name: Ayushman Arogya Mandirs
children.ministry: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare / States
children.spent: Not represented as one national cumulative spend figure here
children.progress: 1.86 lakh+ AAMs functional; cumulative footfall above 540 crore as of Aug 2026.
children.target: Comprehensive primary healthcare close to communities.
children.latest: Government reported continued national expansion in Aug 2026.

children.target: Enable SHG women to earn at least ₹1 lakh per year sustainably for at least four agricultural seasons/business cycles.
children.latest: Government published a national action-plan update in Jul 2026.
